title.justification: The title clearly reflects the main subject of the paper, which is the application of a modified 3D U-Net architecture for brain tumour segmentation.

analysis.description: This paper presents a modified version of the 3D U-Net architecture for brain tumour segmentation using multimodal brain MR volumes. The model is trained on the BraTS 2018 dataset and demonstrates improvements in segmentation tasks, especially in handling class imbalance through a curriculum on class weights.

type.justification: The paper involves experiments with a specific neural network architecture (3D U-Net) on a dataset (BraTS 2018) and presents quantitative results, making it empirical.
type.quote: In this work, we develop a modified version of the popular 3D U-net [13] architecture for brain tumour segmentation task on BraTS 2018 datasets.

name.justification: The paper focuses on brain tumour segmentation, a critical task in medical imaging.
name.quote: In this work, we present a 3D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for brain tumour segmentation from Multimodal brain MR volumes.

name.justification: The paper uses a modified version of a CNN for processing medical images, specifically MRIs, to segment brain tumours.
name.quote: Automatic quantitative analysis of brain tumours assists in better and faster diagnosis procedure and surgical planning.

name.justification: The model is a variant of the popular 3D U-Net architecture, specifically modified for this research.
name.quote: In this work, we develop a modified version of the popular 3D U-net [13] architecture for brain tumour segmentation task on BraTS 2018 datasets.

is_contributed.justification: The paper presents a modified 3D U-net as its primary contribution to the research field.
is_contributed.quote: In this work, we develop a modified version of the popular 3D U-net [13] architecture for brain tumour segmentation task on BraTS 2018 datasets.

is_executed.justification: The model was executed and tested on the BraTS 2018 dataset.
is_executed.quote: The network was trained using a curriculum on class weights to address class imbalance, showing competitive results for brain tumour segmentation on BraTS 2018 [5] testing dataset.

is_compared.justification: The paper includes quantitative comparisons of the modified 3D U-Net's performance on different datasets.
is_compared.quote: We achieved competitive results on BraTS 2018 [5] validation and testing datasets with Dice scores of 0.788, 0.909, and 0.825 on validation dataset, and 0.706, 0.871, and 0.771 on testing dataset for enhancing tumour, whole tumour, and tumour core, respectively.
